Prealgebra · Lesson 3.6

Counting a Number's Divisors

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Lesson 3.1 found that perfect squares alone have an odd divisor count. Lesson 3.3 gave every number a unique prime fingerprint. Now we count a number's divisors straight from that fingerprint, without listing a single one.

Problem
A machine builds divisors of 12=22×312=22×3 by choosing how many 2s (0, 1, or 2) and how many 3s (0 or 1) to multiply together. How many different divisors can it build?
Show a hint
  • You make two separate choices, the number of 22s (three options) and the number of 33s (two options). Every pairing of one choice with the other gives a divisor. Count the pairings.
  • Three options for the 22s and two options for the 33s give 3×23×2 combinations. List them as 2i×3j2i×3j and confirm you get 1,2,3,4,6,121,2,3,4,6,12.
Show the full solution
The 22s can appear 00, 11, or 22 times, which is three choices, and the 33 can appear 00 or 11 times, which is two. The choices are independent, so the divisors number 3×2=6.3×2=6​. Listing them as 2i×3j2i×3j gives 1,2,3,4,6,121,2,3,4,6,12, exactly six. Each prime offers one more choice than its exponent, and independent choices multiply.
Key idea
Add-one-and-multiply rule. If n=pa×qb×⋯n=pa×qb×⋯, the number of positive divisors is (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯. Every divisor is built by choosing how many copies of each prime to take, from 00 up to that prime's exponent, so a prime with exponent aa has a+1a+1 choices. The choices are independent, so the counts multiply.
Problem
The fingerprint of 360 is 360=23×32×5360=23×32×5. Use the add-one-and-multiply rule to count how many positive divisors 360 has without listing them.
Show a hint
  • Each prime contributes one more choice than its exponent. The prime 22 has exponent 33, so it offers 3+13+1 choices. Do the same for 33 and for 55, then multiply.
  • The choice counts are 3+1=43+1=4 for the 22s, 2+1=32+1=3 for the 33s, and 1+1=21+1=2 for the 55. Multiply 4×3×24×3×2.
Show the full solution
Add one to each exponent and multiply. (3+1)(2+1)(1+1)=4×3×2=24.(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)=4×3×2=24​. So 360360 has 2424 positive divisors, found without writing one of them down. The rule handles as many primes as a number carries, turning a long listing chore into a single multiplication.
Problem
Compare 96=25×396=25×3 and 100=22×52100=22×52. Apply the counting rule to each. Which number has more divisors?
Show a hint
  • Apply add-one-and-multiply to each. For 96=25×396=25×3, the counts are 5+15+1 and 1+11+1. For 100=22×52100=22×52, the counts are 2+12+1 and 2+12+1.
  • 9696 gives 6×2=126×2=12 divisors, while 100100 gives 3×3=93×3=9. Which is larger?
Show the full solution
For 96=25×396=25×3, the count is (5+1)(1+1)=6×2=12.(5+1)(1+1)=6×2=12. For 100=22×52100=22×52, it is (2+1)(2+1)=3×3=9.(2+1)(2+1)=3×3=9. The bigger number has fewer divisors, so the answer is 9696​. Divisor count follows the shape of the exponents, not the size of the number. One tall stack of 22s beats two medium stacks here.
Problem
The divisor count (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯ is odd only when every exponent is even, the fingerprint of a perfect square. How many numbers from 1 to 50 have an odd number of divisors?
Show a hint
  • The divisor count is a product (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯. A product of whole numbers is odd only when every single factor in it is odd. So ask, when is every a+1a+1 odd?
  • Every a+1a+1 is odd exactly when every exponent aa is even, which is precisely when the number is a perfect square. So count the perfect squares from 11 to 5050.
Show the full solution
A product of whole numbers is odd only when every factor is odd, and a+1a+1 is odd exactly when aa is even. So an odd divisor count means every exponent is even, which is the fingerprint of a perfect square. From 11 to 5050 the squares are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49,1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, the squares of 11 through 77, since 82=6482=64 overshoots. That is 77​ numbers. This is lesson 3.1's result again, now falling straight out of the counting rule.
Key idea
A number has an odd number of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square. From 3.1, only a perfect square has a factor that pairs with itself, leaving one unpaired. From the counting rule, the product (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯ is odd only when every exponent is even, which happens exactly for perfect squares. The pairing argument and the counting rule give the same answer.
Problem
Find the smallest whole number with exactly 12 divisors by breaking 12 into exponent-plus-one pieces, building the smallest number from each, and comparing.
Show a hint
  • You need (a+1)(b+1)⋯=12(a+1)(b+1)⋯=12. The ways to write 1212 as such a product include 1212, 6×26×2, 4×34×3, and 3×2×23×2×2. Each gives a set of exponents to spend on primes.
  • To keep the number small, give the biggest exponents to the smallest primes. For the split 3×2×23×2×2, that means 22×31×5122×31×51. Build the number for each split and take the least.
  • Compare 211=2048211=2048, 25×3=9625×3=96, 23×32=7223×32=72, and 22×3×5=6022×3×5=60. Which is smallest?
Show the full solution
The exponent-plus-one values have to multiply to 1212, and to keep the number small the biggest exponents go on the smallest primes. 12=12 ⇒ 211=204812=12 ⇒ 211=2048 12=6×2 ⇒ 25×3=9612=6×2 ⇒ 25×3=96 12=4×3 ⇒ 23×32=7212=4×3 ⇒ 23×32=72 12=3×2×2 ⇒ 22×3×5=6012=3×2×2 ⇒ 22×3×5=60 The smallest is 6060​. Spreading the choices across 2,3,52,3,5 is cheaper than stacking them all on 22.
Problem
720=24×32×5720=24×32×5. An even divisor must contain at least one 2. How many even divisors does 720 have?
Show a hint
  • An even divisor must take at least one 22. Normally the 22s offer choices 0,1,2,3,40,1,2,3,4, but forbidding zero 22s leaves only 1,2,3,41,2,3,4. The 33s and the 55 keep all their choices.
  • So the even divisors number 4×(2+1)×(1+1)4×(2+1)×(1+1). Alternatively, count all the divisors and subtract the odd ones, which are the divisors of 32×532×5.
Show the full solution
An even divisor of 720=24×32×5720=24×32×5 must take at least one 22, so the 22s drop from five choices to the four 1,2,3,41,2,3,4. The 33s still give 2+1=32+1=3 and the 55 gives 1+1=21+1=2, so the even divisors number 4×3×2=24.4×3×2=24​. Restricting one prime's choices counts a whole family of divisors directly. Cross-check, 720720 has 3030 divisors and 66 odd ones, and 30−6=2430−6=24.
Fun fact
Highly composite numbers beat every smaller number in divisor count: 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 36, 60, 120, 360. Civilizations pick these for time and angles because many divisors make sharing easy.

Every tool in this chapter came from the same move. Find a number's primes, read the fingerprint, and divisibility, perfect powers, GCD, LCM, and the exact divisor count all follow. Chapter 4 turns to fractions.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A number is given as 24×5224×52. Use the add-one-and-multiply rule to count its positive divisors.
Show the solution
Add one to each exponent and multiply. (4+1)(2+1)=5×3=15.(4+1)(2+1)=5×3=15​. The divisors are 2i×5j2i×5j with ii from 00 to 44 and jj from 00 to 22, which is 55 by 33 pairs.
Practice
Factor 600=23×3×52600=23×3×52 and apply the counting rule. How many positive divisors does 600 have?
Show the solution
Reading the fingerprint 600=23×31×52600=23×31×52, (3+1)(1+1)(2+1)=4×2×3=24.(3+1)(1+1)(2+1)=4×2×3=24​. Once a number is in fingerprint form, its divisor count is one multiplication away.
Practice
Which has more divisors, 64=2664=26 or 90=2×32×590=2×32×5? Count each and enter the number with more.
Show the solution
For 64=2664=26, the count is 6+1=76+1=7. For 90=2×32×590=2×32×5, it is (1+1)(2+1)(1+1)=2×3×2=12(1+1)(2+1)(1+1)=2×3×2=12. So 9090​ has more, twelve against seven. Spreading primes out makes far more divisors than stacking one prime high, so the count tracks fingerprint shape, not size.
Practice
How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 have an odd number of divisors?
Show the solution
A divisor count is odd only when every exponent is even, which means the number is a perfect square. From 11 to 100100 those are 1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100,1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100, the squares of 11 through 1010, so the answer is 1010​. Odd divisor counts belong to perfect squares and nothing else, so counting them is just counting squares.
Practice
Find the smallest whole number with exactly 8 divisors.
Show the solution
The exponent-plus-one values must multiply to 88, and the biggest exponents go on the smallest primes. 8=8 ⇒ 27=128,8=4×2 ⇒ 23×3=24,8=2×2×2 ⇒ 2×3×5=30.8=8 ⇒ 27=128,8=4×2 ⇒ 23×3=24,8=2×2×2 ⇒ 2×3×5=30. The smallest is 2424​, whose divisors are 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,241,2,3,4,6,8,12,24.
Practice
How many positive divisors does 210210 have?
Show the solution
The divisors of 210210 are 20,21,…,21020,21,…,210, one for each exponent from 00 to 1010, so there are 10+1=1110+1=11​. A prime raised to the power aa has a+1a+1 divisors, the simplest case of the rule.
Practice
A number has exactly three divisors only when it is the square of a prime. How many numbers from 1 to 50 have exactly three divisors?
Show the solution
For (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯ to equal 33, and 33 is prime, the product must be the single factor 33. That forces one prime with exponent 22 and nothing else, so the number is a prime squared. Up to 5050 those are 22=4,32=9,52=25,72=49,22=4,32=9,52=25,72=49, since 112=121112=121 overshoots. That is 44​ numbers. The divisors of p2p2 are just 11, pp, and p2p2, which is why three divisors always means a prime square.
Practice
How many of 360's divisors are even, given 360=23×32×5360=23×32×5?
Show the solution
An even divisor needs at least one 22, so the 22s drop from four choices to the three 1,2,31,2,3. The 33s give 2+1=32+1=3 and the 55 gives 1+1=21+1=2, so the even divisors number 3×3×2=18.3×3×2=18​. Cross-check, 360360 has 2424 divisors and 66 odd ones, the divisors of 32×532×5, and 24−6=1824−6=18.
Practice
Divisor counting rule. For n=paqb⋯n=paqb⋯, count is (a+1)(b+1)⋯(a+1)(b+1)⋯. Depends on exponent shape, not size. Odd count ↔ perfect square. Trim one prime's choices for a sub-family. Run backward to design a number with a target count.
Practice
Locker nn is flipped once per divisor, so it ends open only when it has an odd divisor count, exactly the perfect squares. Open lockers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100.
